title: Vocal Affect Bench | Besimple AI
summary: A public benchmark measuring whether AI audio models can identify expressed vocal emotion from raw speech — without transcripts or metadata. Ten baselines. Seven emotion classes. Hopper Audio Perception-1 leads at 59.6%.
body_markdown:
### Emotion matters


A customer who says "that's fine" may be conceding, joking, or signaling frustration. Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models preserve the phrase but strip the vocal delivery that makes the exchange interpretable. Voice agents that apply affect analysis only after transcription measure lexical sentiment — a different question from expressed vocal emotion.


A number of omni and emotion-detection specific models promise to solve this problem. Given an audio clip, these models should be able to detect the correct emotion. How accurate are their predictions?
